comment: Reporting conformance and ICD release adoption — Adds the reporting consequence to release governance. An adopted ICD revision and an annual content release are different; this does not make the newest API release immediately mandatory or impose ICD statistical obligations on every WHO-FIC member. Evidence: WHO Nomenclature Regulations 1967 (https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/who-nomenclature-regulations-1967); WHA72.15 (https://apps.who.int/gb/ebwha/pdf_files/WHA72/A72_R15-en.pdf). Coordinate with A05.01.

Evidence: WHO Nomenclature Regulations 1967 (https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/who-nomenclature-regulations-1967); WHA72.15 (https://apps.who.int/gb/ebwha/pdf_files/WHA72/A72_R15-en.pdf). public.suggestedRevision: Append; retain existing release-testing and transition provisions: For ICD-based statistical reporting, this coordination should identify the applicable ICD revision, release policy, coding rules and transition arrangements needed to meet the Member State's reporting obligations. Proposed changes to WHO content should be routed through WHO's maintenance process. National adoption of a new release should be tested and documented, preserving the reproducibility of earlier reports.
